condition: suspected postoperative pulmonary thromboembolism presenting with abrupt resting inspiratory chest pain 10 days after right clavicle surgery
level_rationale: Abrupt-onset inspiratory chest pain starting while seated at rest 10 days after right collarbone surgery in a 57-year-old adult indicates suspected acute postoperative pulmonary embolism or acute intrathoracic complication requiring immediate emergency department computed tomography pulmonary angiography, electrocardiography, and chest imaging, whereas mild itching along the dry healing surgical scar over that collarbone 10 days postoperatively reflects normal cutaneous wound remodeling appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain postoperative adult lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-site dry healing clavicular scar self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 57, right collarbone surgery 10 days ago, and sudden inspiratory chest pain while seated at rest today) with a 2-word span difference (21 vs 23 words) and zero diagnosis labels ('embolism', 'thrombosis', and 'dvt' omitted from prompt texts). Anchoring f2 to right collarbone surgery keeps the Rule A control in the exact same upper-thoracic/clavicular region when f3 shifts to mild itching along the dry healing collarbone scar (level 4 ER to level 1 home self-care) with zero stranded DVT/PE red flags and zero stated negatives.
